233.t: Losing his brother and best friend
233.s: Monk felt he had lost his best friend and could not relate to music, avoiding even Buddy.
233.ch: Wes's death and Monk's turning point
233.q: : Adjusting to that was, very naturally, one of the hardest adjustments I've ever had to make. Because when I started thinking, it really began to dawn on me how close we were. See, we had never been separated. Even from the early stages, when I was separated from the other parts of my family, Wes…

233.t: Needing to be on his own; his role as the talker
233.s: He wanted independence from Buddy, who depended on him as the talker of the family.
233.ch: Wes's death and Monk's turning point
233.q: Right. I was the one that could get it on, I could get it on. I could walk in a group and be the life of the party. But what was happening, that was I was covering up for the insecurities, making up for the insecurities I had over there. So it balances itself out. But right then, something…

233.t: Buddy says they must go back to work
233.s: After a spell, Buddy phoned that they had to pick up the pieces.
233.ch: Wes's death and Monk's turning point
233.q: : Bud and I were talking, talking and not saying anything, You know what I'm saying? Just talking. We didn't get on every subject and we wouldn't dig up the past. We didn't see much of each other during that period; I really didn't want to see him.

371.t: Recording 'Upon Reflection', the Thad Jones tribute
371.s: The 1993 Verve record with George Mraz and Elvin Jones, a rubato 'A Child Is Born', and Jones says there is never closure after a brother's death.
371.ch: Thad, recent work, outlook and advice
371.q: I mean…not really. You never forget the passing of a close relative, especially like Thad. No matter how many times I play his music, it always brings back memories of him as a person, as an individual, as a family member, as a brother, and as a musician. It evokes memories that you never forget.…

371.t: The loss of Thad and Elvin Jones
371.s: Thad's death in 1986 and later Elvin's were great losses; Thad was recognized in his lifetime.
371.ch: Thad, recent work, outlook and advice
371.q: Well, of course it was a great loss. You had an immediate sense of loss. And lasted even until today. Something happened with Elvin, that was an even greater loss. Elvin was the youngest member of the family, the immediate family. Thad, of course, was a genius just because of his body of work. He…

4.t: Johnny's loss of sight, the 1932 bus accident and the Braille Institute
4.s: Johnny's partial sight ended when a bus hit him in 1932; he died in 1955 and his machine went to the Braille Institute.
4.ch: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
4.q: Well, he was... That was '55, and I was... be 67, wouldn't I? 'Cause I was born in '88, and he was seven years older 'n me, so he'd've been sixty-uh...he'd've been 74.

4.t: What became of Slocum Mitchell and the surviving bandsmen
4.s: Slocum Mitchell died in Los Angeles; Spikes is the last living member of the So Different band and over half of his big band are gone.
4.ch: Later ventures, lodges and San Francisco recollections
4.q: He died. Nearly all the bands did.. All of them boys on the So Different Band--all of them are dead. I'm the only one that's living. Now, on the other band, over half of them's dead.

922.s: His father worked on the roof garden with the Piron band, then died of a heart attack that night.
922.q: Sudden death. Sudden death. It was a heart attack, yeah. He had worked at night up on the roof garden, there was a Peron band there. He was running the place at the time. And up until it was just about 11.30, they were getting ready for a break, because he spoke to me and he said, I want you to get…

152.t: Death of his first wife and mother in 1951
152.s: His wife, who had a heart condition, dropped dead near his mother's house and the shock killed his mother; Earl Palmer pulled him back to the club.
152.ch: Dave Bartholomew band and early recording
152.q: And as a child, she had rheumatic fever that it messed up her heart. Why? And in 1951, she was going to visit my mom and she got two doors from my mom's house and she was... My mom was sitting outside and saw my wife coming and my wife dropped dead and the shock from her killed my mother.

635.t: Kinship with Clarence Williams and his health
635.s: Foster discovers Claiborne Williams was his uncle and that Clarence Williams is a relative; they talk about Clarence's stroke, shop and marriage.
635.q: No, she, she, oh, she didn't have been separated a long time. Well, they had been, I don't know.

1006.t: Lee Collins arrives in New Orleans
1006.s: Lee Collins is said to be powerful; Alexis recalls his stopping at a hotel and calling, when Alexis was alone after his wife and mother died.
1006.q: Yes, when Lee came here, he stopped at this hotel on Belmont Street, and he called up his house. My wife and my mother got killed in my car. I was living here alone.

270.t: Claiborne Williams as teacher and his brother George's fatal illness
270.s: He compares Claiborne Williams to Dave Perkins as a teacher of both races, and tells his father's story of Claiborne's travelling brother George, a trombonist who died after a pneumonia while Claiborne nursed him.
270.q: Yeah. Mm-hmm . Mm-hmm . And Claiborne, I would say, was like when I came to New Orleans, like Dave Poikin was. He taught both white and colored. Because I remember there was a white student and he had to go to their house and teach them, you see. And he was very known, I mean, as a very good…

574.s: Robinson says he has just lost his wife; Russell attended the wake at Blandin's.
574.q: Yeah. That's what he heard. It didn't have been so long. It just didn't look like I forgot the air and everything. Then my mind ain't all so far enough. You know I just lose my wife.

1007.t: Losing Davern, Tony Scott and Ahmet Ertegun; Davern's last years
1007.s: After the deaths he grieved, then took more responsibility for his own music and community. He thinks Davern was strong but losing friends such as Tony DiNicola amid fewer good jobs.
1007.q: At the same time, when he died and also when Tony Scott died, it was shortly in that same period. And another good friend, Ahmet Ertegun when those guys passed away I did go through a period where I was feeling pretty sorry for myself and I had a friend remind me, how old are you? Meaning, really?…

353.t: Losing her son and brother; faith and church
353.s: Redd speaks of her mother's death, her son's death in 1996, her brother's recent death, therapy, prayer and her church.
353.q: I can say this, when I retired from teaching school you know I taught a long time, and my family’s just — my mother went ‘92, then I went to Europe in ’94, and I said well I’m out of school now I can get back to really performing. Then my son was taken sick and he passed in ’96. And oh God, that…

494.s: Bill died of cancer in 1989 and kept teaching from his hospital bed.
494.q: Sure, yeah. He – it was kind of a surprise. Well, not really a surprise. He had gotten sick some months before that. He was in the hospital. A couple of years before that, he had a heart attack. But that wasn’t the cause. It was cancer, something with platelets. He had gotten sick in New York, and…

153.t: Pearl Bailey's death in Philadelphia in 1990
153.s: He describes Pearl's sudden collapse from a heart condition at the Philadelphia Holiday Inn, her death and his memories of her generosity.
153.ch: Arranging, bandleading and Pearl Bailey's life
153.q: She was born in Newport News, Virginia, but spent a lot of time in Philadelphia and Washington, D.C. – those two places.

527.t: Twinship, fate and being reconciled before Addison died
527.s: Farmer reflects on the closeness of twins and gratitude for the reconciliation.
527.q: Yeah, right. February 23rd, something like that. So, you really can’t take anything for granted. You’re just out here, the whims of fate. You do the best you can do. Don’t be a fool and jump in front of a car and figure it’s not my time to go [laughs]. I’m just grateful that we had come back…

111.t: His mother's heart disease and death
111.s: His mother, with heart disease, died on the stairs on Thanksgiving three years after his father.
111.ch: Sideman years: J.J., Tyree Glenn, Sweets
111.q: She had a bad—she had a lot of – she had heart disease. She just gradually got more and more feeble and she wasn’t able to get around as much. But she never stopped cleaning the house and she was up and down the stairs, she cooked all the time. One day I wasn’t staying home, I was in Detroit, I was…

565.t: Charlie's death and the Count title
565.s: He remembers Charlie's death in 1988 and their joke about the family title.
565.ch: Charlie, critics and the Latin Jazz Grammy
565.q: he was 60 years young. And left a vacuum, and changed my whole thing around, my life... He was my main everything. The greatest friend I could have ever had. The greatest brother that I DID have, but my friend. Friend. You can be a brother and not be your friend. I loved him so much, man. We had…

705.s: Asked about a Japanese-feeling piece, he describes his sister, her death and burial on September 11, 2001, and the invitation to play in Japan.
705.q: Oh my god yes. Japanese experience, wow! That’s very deep. I have to back a little bit on that. I have one sister, no brothers. My sister was five years older than me. She was my boss, you know? When I was younger, despite my physical size, if anybody messed with me I’d get my sister. She was…

102.t: Pat Patrick's illness and his father
102.s: He recalls Pat Patrick, dying of cancer, thanking him for the Moody job, and wishes to speak to Patrick's father.
102.q: That’s the way Moody ties in with the Pat Patrick story. Now it turns out that Pat Patrick has a father. More than that, when Pat Patrick was dying, he came by the house and brought his father because he was looking for some alternative methods for dealing with cancer. So, I had run around and…

67.t: The death of Princess White on stage at 95
67.s: Cheatham was at the concert near Larchmont where Princess White sang Peeping Through the Keyhole, said she felt tired, and died.
67.ch: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
67.q: Well she sang very well. She sang all of her songs, the last song was 'Peeping Through the Keyhole.' That was the last song, she sang it without any prob-

68.t: His son's cancer and death in Silver Spring
68.s: The son, a health-conscious engineer, is found to have cancer of the lung and liver and dies within weeks; Tate carries on playing in Europe.
68.q: So he was jogging, he ran down under the hill and he told me he was completely exhausted when he got down to the bottom of that hill. He couldn't get back up. He told me he

378.t: Dance's afterword: Mildred's last phone call
378.s: Dance adds that Red stayed close to Mildred and her last call that night was to him.
378.ch: Las Vegas, Sinatra and later years
378.q: Well -- JR the one thing -- Red has gone, and I remember the one thing I did want to get down on tape, which I forgot to ask him about or which I think you probably know, but it's worth mentioning, I think, and that was further to his relationship with Mildred, they remained close friends, I guess…

452.t: His mother's final illness and death in December 1975
452.s: Cobb speaks of his mother as wise confidant who came to live with him after his wife died, her stroke in November 1975 and death on December 17, and her protectiveness of him.
452.ch: Europe tours, Birdland memories and closing
452.q: Told you about the Carnegie Hall situation, the Ralph Cooper situation and blah, blah, blah and about my mother. You know, after my wife died, I brought my mother out there with me, and she took care of me. But she was a woman of great understanding. And anytime I'd get depressed or have any…

147.t: Hot Lips Page and his wife Elizabeth's cremation
147.s: Crawford remembers Page as a warm man who came to talk to him, and relates how Page's former wife was cremated.
147.ch: Precision, the union and learning to read
147.q: Beautiful. That man, you know what he used to do, Stan? Like, he'd see me sitting across the street from the hotel, on a stoop, old concrete stoop, legs stretched out on the sidewalk. You know, Lips would make it a point to come by and sit and talk with me and give me advice, and tell me the things…

95.t: "After My Laughter Came Tears" and the man she lived with after her husband
95.s: She sings a song that fits her life and talks about her husband's death and a long relationship with another Buddy, who died of a heart attack.
95.q: Now, here's a song I like, I know somebody else wrote it, but the song fits me to a tee. See my man, my husband died, the story of it piqued me. I told people, I don't care what you've got (unintelligible).

388.t: Deaths of Tommy and Jimmy Dorsey
388.s: Tommy Dorsey chokes on food and dies, and about a year later Jimmy dies of cancer; Leeman sends a telegram to his hospital room.
388.ch: Honors, Gibson and Dorsey late years
388.q: It wasn't long after that that Tommy Dorsey choked on some food while he was sleeping and died, and it was no more than ayear later that my dear friend, Jimmy, died in I think it was St. Claire Hospital, New York, of cancer.

239.s: Jones describes the memorial for his wife Violet Speedy, with Sarah singing and lighting by Carl Carruthers.
239.q: We even had the lighting set up. You know, because Carl Carruthers, who used to do the lights for Sammy Davis, Jr. and Count Basie, went there early and had pin, red and white lights. He set the whole thing up, you know.
